subject: PulseAI renewal — utilization reconciliation & staged GPU add

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Renewal discussion — utilization reconciliation & staged GPU add

Hi Alex and Samira,

Thanks again for taking time last week. As we approach your November renewal, I pulled a utilization reconciliation for your Dedicated fleet and sketched a low-risk staged add to prevent tail latency events you flagged. The attached CSV has the month-by-month slot usage, and the spreadsheet shows three sizing scenarios.

High level summary:
- 90-day average utilization across your committed pool: 58%
- 95th/99th percentile tail events push cluster utilization above 90% during peak windows (model retrains + high-concurrency inference)
- Observed median queue delay during tail windows: ~380ms additional request latency

Proposed immediate path (short): provision a 25-GPU burst pool to absorb peaks and configure an automatic conversion to committed capacity for 15 GPUs after a 60-day verification window if utilization stays >70% sustained. That protects you from immediate latency while keeping the committed uplift conservative.

I attached: PulseAIMonthlyUtilization_May-Aug.csv and a staged addendum draft (staged-addendum-v2.pdf). Can you confirm which internal stakeholders should receive the PO? Also, any constraints from procurement on staged add/convert language?

Next steps I suggest:
1) We run the burst pool for 30 days while we collect telemetry.
2) After 60 days, if sustained utilization criteria met, convert 15 GPUs to committed slots on an amended contract.
3) Redwood will provide a canary rollback plan and 24/7 escalation channel during the activation window.

Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the numbers.

Best,
Rachel Kim

Alex — quick answers inline and attached a per-workload slice export. See redwood-staged-add-plan.xlsx for the math.

1) Workload breakout (last 60 days):
   - Inference steady-state consumption: ~62% of committed token-hours (primarily conversational models)
   - Scheduled retrains/batch jobs: ~28% of peak hour consumption but concentrated into 6 windows/month
   - Ad-hoc experimentation: ~10% (non-critical; can be scheduled)

2) Billing for burst pool: non-committed; pay-as-you-go on top of your existing invoice. We will invoice monthly for burst usage at the burst rate. If you convert GPUs to committed, we will credit prior burst spend pro rata against the commit for the conversion window per the addendum.

3) Conversion notice/cancellation: conversion to commit requires a 14-day notice prior to the conversion effective date. Once converted, committed GPUs are subject to the committed minimum term in your renewal addendum (standard 12 months). We can build a phased conversion to mitigate risk.

Cost delta examples (attached sheet):
- Conservative: convert 10 GPUs to commit after 60 days. Estimated spend delta vs current term: +12% annualized.
- Aggressive: convert 15 GPUs to commit after 60 days. Estimated spend delta: +18% annualized, with expected latency reduction of ~25% on tail windows.

If that looks reasonable I can loop David on the operational plan and Ben on the commercial terms.

—Rachel

Subject: PulseAI — staged-add operational plan and next steps

Hi Alex/Samira — attaching the operational runbook and the exact thresholds you asked for. Summary below. Attachment: redwood-staged-add-plan.xlsx, staged-addendum-v2.pdf.

Operational highlights:
- Burst pool: 25 x NVIDIA A100-equivalent slots provisioned in your region (us-west-2) as non-committed burst capacity.
- Autoscale trigger: sustained cluster CPU+GPU utilization > 72% for a rolling 10-minute window AND request queue depth above 60% of baseline for 5 consecutive minutes.
- Canary: route 25% of production inference traffic to the expanded pool for first 48 hours. Validate 99th percentile latency improvement and error rates.
- Commit conversion policy: if after 60 days the rolling 14-day average utilization of the additional 25 slots is >70% AND 99th percentile tail events reduced by at least 15%, convert 15 GPUs to committed capacity. Conversion requires 14 days notice once both criteria met.
- Rollback: disable conversion; drain added slots; revert traffic routing in under 30 minutes. If catastrophic failure, we have hot fallback to your previous commit and Redwood will open an incident and provide 4-hour remediation SLA for the first 72 hours post-activation.

Financials (high level):
- Monthly forecasted incremental spend (burst-only test): ~$48k/mo
- Conservative conversion (10 GPUs): annualized +12% vs current runrate
- Aggressive conversion (15 GPUs): annualized +18% vs current runrate

Next steps:
1) Please confirm the PO contact and whether you want the burst charge to be billed to the existing contract or as a standalone line.
2) If approved, sign the attached staged-addendum-v2.pdf; I will provision the burst pool within 48 hours of receiving signed addendum and PO.
3) We will schedule a 30-minute kickoff with your infra and our SREs to confirm routing and canary parameters.

DocuSign link (addendum): https://docusign.com/doc/PAI-DEAL-4721-staged
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deal/DEAL-4721

Happy to discuss on a call this afternoon if helpful.
